notes: Reduced kp gain to 8 for smoother steering and decreased oscillation. Shifted sensor x-positions outward by ±0.01 m to better cover sharp turns on slalom track, aiming to reduce line loss events and improve finish rates. rationale: The previous iteration's evidence shows that increasing sensor size to 0.016 m and shifting sensors forward by +0.01 m improved line coverage and early detection, reducing line loss events on oval and s-bend tracks. However, the slalom track still has zero finish rate, high line loss events (0.9), and elevated steering oscillation (0.398), indicating difficulty with sharp turns and control stability. To address this, I reduced the proportional gain kp from 10 to 8 to smooth steering control and decrease oscillation. Additionally, I adjusted the sensor x-positions outward by ±0.01 m to better cover sharp turns on the slalom track, aiming to reduce line loss events and improve finish rates. Sensor size and forward y-positions remain unchanged to preserve early line detection benefits. The controller uses PID gains tuned for smoother control, with sensor weights emphasizing outer sensors for edge detection. The line loss recovery strategy remains 'search_left' to steer right when the line is lost. Observation requests include completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, steering_oscillation, and control_effort to monitor performance and control smoothness comprehensively.
